why: Nothing independently monitors the chain today, and tamper-evidence is only a guarantee if a party other than the writer scans it.
An aspect of the errors capability: RFC 9457 already supplies the container, and what is missing is the platform's own registered type set, which belongs in cap-errors' closed registry.
The ordered chain of typed slots every unit passes through is the placement that makes the seven cross-cutting concerns undeclinable.
An aspect of the delegation placement rule: the binding point is entry, before any planning or spend.
T1.2 needs the platform to be entered by an external agent, which is the opposite direction from cap-agent-runtime and is served rather than consumed.

The eighth design rule and its three counts (concepts to a first run, resident metadata per unit, required fields for a minimum implementation) are a build discipline, not an area of the platform; T3 makes it checkable rather than aspirational.

Duplicates cap-identity entirely: attest and delegate are exactly the SVID plus RFC 8693 token exchange that cap-identity already names as its standard and purpose, and recording the chain is xc-identity-delegation's stated job. The one detail worth keeping, the delegated attestation path, is noted on cap-identity.
Merged: the required per-adapter mapping and the byte-identical-envelope conformance test are the same seam stated from the intake side.
Per-call version declaration, a frozen core field set and a stated deprecation window apply to every capability interface at once, so they belong to the build layer rather than to any one interface.
Resolution by name and version constraint over signed, content-addressed records is missing; cap-capability-packaging covers the file shape only.
Declaring an irreversibility class and a compensating step is new: the existing idempotency skills cover the lease, not what to do when the effect cannot be replayed away.
A closed set of deterministic operators is where cross-cutting concerns attach and is the vocabulary the Document's steps use; no existing compose- skill defines it.
Same requirement as the entry conformance suite seen from the developer-experience side: drive a full task from a generated client with no repository code on the caller side.
An aspect of the Dispatch request and result: declared input context, a declared folded summary, and compaction as a recorded transition.
xc-correlation states that correlation must be explicit; nothing names the field set or the carrier per boundary, which is what leaves each new boundary to invent one.
Identity and secrets are different problems: SPIFFE/SPIRE manages no tokens or keys, so brokering short-lived audience-bound credentials needs its own capability.

An aspect of the Dispatch contract: step id, idempotency key, checkpoint reference and a replay semantic satisfiable by both a durable engine and a queue plus a state machine.
An aspect of the definition-of-done discipline: report which stages were applicable, and attest the configuration actually resolved rather than the file supplied.
Merged with the OpenAPI/AsyncAPI conformance check: one suite proving all three actors enter with third-party tooling, with a deliberately broken adapter it must fail on.
One record every driving adapter produces, read by all routing and all cross-cutting concerns, is the boundary TARGET.md T1 and T2.3 both rest on.
Merged: the entry gate is the admission slot of the same chain, and adopting a protocol must not bypass it.
Offline scoring against a versioned dataset and baseline is distinct from the runtime Judge and has no home in the manifest.
An aspect of the Document's definition of done: runnable checks with risk tiers, and inconclusive rather than passed when no behavioural check ran.
PASS.md B3 has no human-interaction row at all; the waiting-for-human state with approve, edit, reject-with-notes and partial acceptance is the missing capability.

An aspect of the idempotency capability: the claim/duplicate/conflict return triple and the typed-conflict MUST are its operation signature.
TARGET.md T4.4 requires a loop that revises the producing skills and promotes only on evidence; compose-loop bounds an iteration but changes nothing about the skill.

An extension of the Judge, not a new area: criterion sampling and a held-out gold-judge audit strengthen design rule 6 in place.
An aspect of the lease placement rule: per-adapter key derivation and attach-to-in-flight on duplicate.

No existing skill gives an agent scoped, retrievable memory; the Ledger is a dedup authority, not memory.

Same split from the entry lens: pin the convention in the adapter and keep the platform's correlation fields independent of it.

An aspect of the State seam: expectedVersion append, snapshots, named projections and Merkle proofs alongside the existing hash chain.
A mandatory principal verified at every shared choke point, with per-principal quotas and prefixed storage keys, is absent from PASS.md and from the manifest.
An aspect of the provenance capability: two predicates, build-shaped and run-shaped, behind one in-toto/DSSE envelope so one verifier handles both.
An aspect of packaging: the three tiers are already this skill's shape; the budgets go to build-simplicity-budget and publication to cap-capability-registry.
